questions.text: For what cause did Paul leave Titus in Crete (Titus 1:5)?

options.text: To gather silver for the poor and carry it unto the saints at Jerusalem
That he should set in order things wanting, and ordain elders in every city
To build a synagogue on Crete and order the daily ministering of priests
To escape from secular magistrates and seek quiet refuge upon the island

questions.text: What family qualification is required of an elder in Titus 1:6?

options.text: An unmarried brother that hath no children of his own
A father of at least five sons walking in all gravity
The husband of one wife, having faithful, sober children
A kinsman of an honourable priestly lineage in Judea

questions.text: What must the bishop hold fast according to Titus 1:9?

options.text: To the traditions of ancient Greek philosophers
To the civil statutes of the Roman province laws
To the cunning fables and poetry of the heathen
Holding fast the faithful word as he was taught

questions.text: What witness did a prophet of their own say concerning the Cretians (Titus 1:12)?

options.text: The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies
The Cretians are alway true, full of mercy and diligence
The Cretians are the devoutest nation upon the earth
The Cretians are faithful brethren and models of virtue

questions.text: What is written concerning the pure and the defiled in Titus 1:15?

options.text: Unto all men without difference all earthly things are pure by nature
Unto the pure all things are pure: but to the defiled is nothing pure
Unto the defiled all things are pure, but to the righteous all is sin
Unto all believers all meats remain unclean until they be sanctified

questions.text: What should the aged women teach the young women in Titus 2:4-5?

options.text: To seek after worldly dominion and proudly exalt themselves above others
To command their husbands and rule over the entire household with power
To love their husbands and children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home
To forsake all domestic duties and dwell in complete worldly liberty

questions.text: In what manner should Titus shew himself in all things (Titus 2:7)?

options.text: A follower of wise men
A judge over the heathen
A pleader in worldly law
A pattern of good works

questions.text: How should servants behave toward their own masters (Titus 2:9-10)?

options.text: Obedient unto their masters, not answering again, showing fidelity
Resisting their masters continually and seeking secret worldly gain
Forsaking their manual labour because all are free brethren in faith
Reproaching their masters with anger and demanding immediate freedom

questions.text: What does the grace of God teach us in Titus 2:12?

options.text: To gather abundance of gold and lead an easy, carefree life upon the earth
That, denying worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly
To despise civil magistrates and withdraw entirely from communion with men
To flee from all tribulation and hide ourselves in solitary mountain dens

questions.text: What are believers looking for according to Titus 2:13?

options.text: For the building of an earthly palace and the spread of an earthly kingdom
For the rising of an earthly king and the establishment of temporal peace
For that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of our great God and Lord
For the immediate cessation of manual labour and permanent rest from men

questions.text: How should believers be minded toward principalities and powers (Titus 3:1)?

options.text: Resist with violent sedition whenever civil statutes seem unjust
Display total indifference and disregard the decrees of rulers
Obey only when the magistrates themselves confess the true faith
Be subject to powers, obey magistrates, ready to every good work

questions.text: By what means did God according to His mercy save us in Titus 3:5?

options.text: By the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost
By works of righteousness which we ourselves had previously done
By the exact observance of all ancestral rites taught by fathers
By human philosophy and subtle knowledge received from the Greeks

questions.text: To what end being justified by His grace were we made in Titus 3:7?

options.text: That we might become worldly potentates and reign over heathen kings
That we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life
That we might search out subtle contentions and genealogies of men
That we might gain earthly fame and temporal praise before all people

questions.text: What should be done unto a man that is an heretic in Titus 3:10?

options.text: Promote him straightway into a high office in the flock
Implead him before the secular magistrates of the city
After the first and second admonition reject that man
Suffer him without any rebuke to continue his speeches

questions.text: In what city did Paul determine to winter (Titus 3:12)?

options.text: At the city of Troas
At the city of Rome
At the city of Athens
At the city of Nicopolis
